classification.difficultyReason: Recognise equivalent rays but distinguish segments with different endpoints and explain the difference.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Name a ray that is the same as the ray PQ.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 3, below part a and right of centre, above part b
spec.description: A rising diagonal line with arrows beyond both end points and labelled points P, Q, R in that order; labels sit below-right.
spec.mathematics: P, Q and R are collinear, with Q between P and R. Both arrows are retained. No equal-length relationship is asserted by the illustrative spacing.
spec.answerVisibility: Shared question evidence for parts a and b; no supplied answer text is drawn.

answer.worked: Q and R lie in the same direction from P. Rays PQ and PR have the same endpoint and direction.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Joseph says line segment $PQ$ is the same as line segment $PR$. Explain why he is incorrect.

answer.short: The line segments are different lengths.
answer.worked: Q lies between P and R, so segment PR contains segment PQ and the additional segment QR. Therefore PR is longer than PQ; the segments also have different endpoints.
